svg.title: Four Checks Before Irreversible Exposure
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-05-rights-statutes-and-site-checks; chart type: decision_tree; title: Four Checks Before Irreversible Exposure; subtitle: Proceed on documented evidence; resolve defects or reject the parcel; chapter number: 5; epistemic tag: operating_framework; assumptions note: These four sequential checks apply according to transaction type and jurisdiction. A failed check routes the opportunity to documented remediation or rejection, not automatic execution. Cited provisions establish specific requirements or frameworks; they do not replace parcel-level determinations.; caption: Capital follows confirmed capacity, priority, permitted use, and site condition. A favorable exit multiple cannot repair an unassignable right or prohibited yard operation.; stages: label: Capacity and licensed activity; value: Proceed if transaction role is verified; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Map principal activity, options, referrals, and services performed for others against the applicable state rules. California Business and Professions Code 10130 and 10131 illustrate the licensing boundary; do not assume every option assignment qualifies for an exemption.; label: Priority and required consents; value: Proceed if enforceable rights survive; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Inspect title, mortgage priority, termination clauses, assignment restrictions, and access easements. Obtain required lender and lessor consents and negotiate an effective SNDA where needed; the SNDA requirement depends on documents and risk, not a universal statute.; label: Sign and telecom permissions; value: Proceed if the proposed use is permitted; numeric value: 3.0; detail: For covered highway signs, apply 23 U.S.C. 131, 23 CFR 750.705–750.706, state DOT spacing criteria, and local digital-sign rules. For telecom, check 47 CFR 17.4 applicability and local siting requirements within 47 U.S.C. 332(c)(7).; label: IOS environmental and axle suitability; value: Proceed if site obligations are costed; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Before executing the master lease, obtain Phase I screening and verify heavy-vehicle zoning, turning paths, surface capacity, drainage, and fire access. Scope 40 CFR Part 312 when applicable and assess industrial stormwater coverage under 40 CFR 122.26.

rect.title: label: Capacity and licensed activity; value: Proceed if transaction role is verified; numeric value: 1.0; detail: Map principal activity, options, referrals, and services performed for others against the applicable state rules. California Business and Professions Code 10130 and 10131 illustrate the licensing boundary; do not assume every option assignment qualifies for an exemption.

text.title: Map principal activity, options, referrals, and services performed for others against the applicable state rules. California Business and Professions Code 10130 and 10131 illustrate the licensing boundary; do not assume every option assignment qualifies for an exemption.

rect.title: label: Priority and required consents; value: Proceed if enforceable rights survive; numeric value: 2.0; detail: Inspect title, mortgage priority, termination clauses, assignment restrictions, and access easements. Obtain required lender and lessor consents and negotiate an effective SNDA where needed; the SNDA requirement depends on documents and risk, not a universal statute.

text.title: Inspect title, mortgage priority, termination clauses, assignment restrictions, and access easements. Obtain required lender and lessor consents and negotiate an effective SNDA where needed; the SNDA requirement depends on documents and risk, not a universal statute.

rect.title: label: Sign and telecom permissions; value: Proceed if the proposed use is permitted; numeric value: 3.0; detail: For covered highway signs, apply 23 U.S.C. 131, 23 CFR 750.705–750.706, state DOT spacing criteria, and local digital-sign rules. For telecom, check 47 CFR 17.4 applicability and local siting requirements within 47 U.S.C. 332(c)(7).

text.title: For covered highway signs, apply 23 U.S.C. 131, 23 CFR 750.705–750.706, state DOT spacing criteria, and local digital-sign rules. For telecom, check 47 CFR 17.4 applicability and local siting requirements within 47 U.S.C. 332(c)(7).

rect.title: label: IOS environmental and axle suitability; value: Proceed if site obligations are costed; numeric value: 4.0; detail: Before executing the master lease, obtain Phase I screening and verify heavy-vehicle zoning, turning paths, surface capacity, drainage, and fire access. Scope 40 CFR Part 312 when applicable and assess industrial stormwater coverage under 40 CFR 122.26.

text.title: Before executing the master lease, obtain Phase I screening and verify heavy-vehicle zoning, turning paths, surface capacity, drainage, and fire access. Scope 40 CFR Part 312 when applicable and assess industrial stormwater coverage under 40 CFR 122.26.

Assumptions: These four sequential checks apply according to transaction type and jurisdiction. A failed check routes the opportunity to documented remediation or rejection, not automatic execution. Cited provisions establish specific requirements or frameworks; they do not replace parcel-level determinations.
